title: Replacing an empty document keeps the comment on the start marker line
notes: The document has a start marker with a comment and no content, so its root is empty (null). Replacing the whole document (the empty path, RFC 6902 section 4.3) makes the root a mapping, written after the marker line. The comment is on the marker line, outside the node, and edits do not touch comments outside the value (docs/edit-semantics.md, Comments). A block mapping or a flow mapping `{a: 1}` both read back as the new value, and the specification allows both, so the choice of a block mapping on the next line at indentation 0 is a convention.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that dropped the comment on the start marker line when it wrote the content of an empty document.
